cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Leave the director's name on the launch programme. The department heads need someone above them. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her resignation is in the printer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Put it in my drawer. Without her, they'll each claim the launch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're asking which of them gets her opening speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read it on her behalf. Give them equal introductions; nobody inherits the microphone.

mechanism: A confidently manages a launch while concealing the director resignation and accommodating equal departmental roles to preserve the existing balance above competing heads.
confusable: Unlike hiding personal fault, A explicitly protects the power arrangement from competing claims; borrowed authority must keep the organizers cooperative with that concealment.
comparison: Absent director and opening speech differ from a chair expenditure problem and a private funding fix.
seedUse: Use D63-a resignation/programme/equal introductions with S02-a adopting other participants needs as an orderly event plan.
